title: Know what is available, issued, and expiring

scenes.title: Know what is available, issued, and expiring
scenes.narration: Welcome to Resgrid Academy. In this lesson, we will know what is available, issued, and expiring. Unrecorded transfers and missing expiry dates make stock levels unreliable and replenishment harder to plan. We will explain the features, the setup decisions, and a practical way to check the result.

scenes.title: A department scenario
scenes.narration: Medical supplies are tracked by lot with expiry alerts, and turnout gear is issued to members. Know what you have, where it is and what is about to expire. The examples in this series use a fictional department and are teaching scenarios, not default settings.

scenes.title: Inventory
scenes.narration: Inventory. Items, stock levels and storage locations. Add the supplies and equipment you track and where they are stored. Availability also depends on Inventory. Check access in the target department.

scenes.title: Inventory counts, expiry and alerts
scenes.narration: Inventory counts, expiry and alerts. Counts, expiry dates and low-stock alerts. Set minimum levels and expiry alerts for critical supplies. Availability also depends on Inventory. Check access in the target department.

scenes.title: Inventory Status
scenes.narration: Inventory Status. What is on hand, running low or expiring. Decide which supplies and equipment are worth tracking and where they are stored. Availability also depends on Inventory. Check access in the target department.

scenes.title: Transfer Inventory
scenes.narration: Transfer Inventory. Move stock between locations. Decide which supplies and equipment are worth tracking and where they are stored. Availability also depends on Inventory. Check access in the target department.

scenes.title: Issue Equipment
scenes.narration: Issue Equipment. Issue equipment to members and record returns. Decide which supplies and equipment are worth tracking and where they are stored. Availability also depends on Inventory. Check access in the target department.

scenes.title: Inventory purchasing
scenes.narration: Inventory purchasing. Suppliers, purchase orders and deliveries. Decide which supplies and equipment are worth tracking and where they are stored. Availability also depends on Inventory. Check access in the target department.

scenes.title: Configure one useful workflow
scenes.narration: For the training scenario, work in this order. Step 1. Define the stock locations and items the department will track. Step 2. Record a receipt, transfer, and equipment issue using sample stock. Step 3. Review counts, expiry, low-stock alerts, and purchasing needs.

scenes.title: Verify the result
scenes.narration: Now verify the result. Reconcile a physical demo count with recorded stock. Check the destination of a transfer, the equipment assignee, and the expiry record. A common problem to watch for: A purchase order is distinct from a received delivery. Reconcile the receipt before assuming stock is available.

scenes.title: Try it with your department
scenes.narration: Your practice task is simple. Receive ten demo supplies, transfer two, and issue one durable item. Reconcile the resulting balances and inspect expiry alerts. Record the result, who owns the follow-up, and when it should be reviewed. Use the linked feature scripts for the detailed screen recording plan.
